It is only safe to choose not to write to a bad block if that bad
block is safely recorded in metadata - i.e. if it has been
'acknowledged'.
If it hasn't we need to wait for the acknowledgement.
We support that using rdev->blocked wait and
md_wait_for_blocked_rdev by introducing a new device flag
'BlockedBadBlock'.
This flag is only advisory.
It is cleared whenever we acknowledge a bad block
can re-check the particular bad blocks that it is interested it.
It should be set by a caller when they find they need to wait.
This (set after test) is inherently racy
md_wait_for_blocked_rdev already has a timeout
have minimal impact.
When we clear ""Blocked"" was also clear ""BlockedBadBlocks"" incase it
was set incorrectly (see above race).
We also modify the way we manage 'Blocked' to fit better with the new
handling of 'BlockedBadBlocks' and to make it consistent between
externally managed and internally managed metadata.   This requires
that each raidXd loop checks if the metadata needs to be written and
triggers a write (md_check_recovery) if needed.  Otherwise a queued
write request might cause raidXd to wait for the metadata to write
and only that thread can write it.
Before writing metadata
column2: we set FaultRecorded for all devices that

column1: are Faulty
column2: then after writing the metadata we clear Blocked for any

column1: device for which the Fault was certainly Recorded.
The 'faulty' device flag now appears in sysfs if the device is faulty
*or* it has unacknowledged bad blocks.  So user-space which does not
understand bad blocks can continue to function correctly.
User space which does
column2: should not assume a device is faulty until it

column1: sees the 'faulty' flag
column2: and then sees the list of unacknowledged bad

column1: blocks is empty.
